beats.primary: The Source of Serenity

beats.label: The Cave
beats.primary: Hunted out of Mecca, the Prophet ﷺ hid in a cave with his closest friend. The searchers came so close that Abu Bakr said: if one of them looks down, he will see us. The Prophet ﷺ was unshaken.

beats.label: The Cave
beats.primary: He answered: "What do you think of two, the third of whom is Allah? Do not worry — Allah is certainly with us."

beats.label: The Cave
beats.primary: And Allah sent down His serenity upon him. The danger was still outside — the stillness inside was real.
Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find comfort.

beats.label: catalog id 11, verbatim
beats.primary: The Ever-Forgiving

beats.label: The servant who kept returning
beats.primary: A man sinned, and said: my Lord, I have sinned — forgive me. And he was forgiven. Time passed, and he fell again.

beats.label: The servant who kept returning
beats.primary: Again he asked. Again he was forgiven. And a third time — Allah answered that His servant knew he had a Lord who forgives, and He forgave him.

beats.label: The servant who kept returning
beats.primary: In the story, the loop you are ashamed of ends the same way every time — not at the sin, but at the return.
O My servants who have exceeded the limits against their souls! Do not lose hope in Allah's mercy, for Allah certainly forgives all sins.

beats.label: The man who took a hundred lives
beats.primary: A man of an earlier nation had taken ninety-nine lives. He asked: is repentance possible for me? He was told no — and the count became one hundred. Still, he kept asking.

beats.label: The man who took a hundred lives
beats.primary: Then he was told: go to a righteous town. He set out — and died on the road, still on his way.

beats.label: The man who took a hundred lives
beats.primary: The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. And the earth was commanded to draw the town closer — he was found a single span nearer to it, and forgiven.

beats.primary: Allah said: "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste." He was not corrected. He was given something to do, and told what would happen.
"Is not that [Creator] Able to give life to the dead?"

beats.label: catalog 75, verbatim
beats.primary: O Capable, nothing is beyond Your power. Fulfill my need and help me with what has left me helpless.
beats.arabic: يَا قَادِرُ لَا يَعْجِزُكَ شَيْءٌ فَاقْضِ لِي حَاجَتِي وَأَعِنِّي عَلَى مَا أَعْجَزَنِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Qadir, la ya'jizuka shay' faqdhi li hajati wa-a'inni 'ala ma a'jazani

beats.primary: He already believed. He asked to be shown anyway — and what came back was not a rebuke, it was four birds and a hill.

beats.primary: There was a stretch where you stopped doing the thing you used to do. Something in you decided that meant you had been dropped.

beats.label: catalog id 16, verbatim
beats.primary: The Self-Sustaining

beats.label: The night nobody woke
beats.primary: They stopped to sleep on the road, and Bilāl was the one who said he would keep them awake. "Bilal rested his back against his Rahila and he too was overwhelmed (by sleep) and slept."

beats.label: The night nobody woke
beats.primary: They woke to the sun already up. Bilāl said: "I have never slept such a sleep." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah captured your souls when He wished, and released them when He wished."

beats.label: The night nobody woke
beats.primary: The Qur'ān says it of every sleeper: "Allāh takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term…"
"Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep."

beats.label: catalog 16, verbatim
beats.primary: O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, in Your mercy I seek help. Rectify all my affairs and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye.
beats.arabic: يَا حَيُّ يَا قَيُّومُ بِرَحْمَتِكَ أَسْتَغِيثُ أَصْلِحْ لِي شَأْنِي كُلَّهُ وَلَا تَكِلْنِي إِلَى نَفْسِي طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ
beats.transliteration: Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum, bi-rahmatika astagheeth, aslih li sha'ni kullahu wa la takilni ila nafsi tarfata 'ayn

beats.primary: The gap was in what you were doing, not in what was holding you up. Nothing that keeps you has ever needed a night off.

beats.primary: There is a mercy that keeps everyone alive. And there is a mercy that answers. This is the Name for the second one.

beats.label: from `collectible_names.json` id 3, verbatim
beats.primary: The Most Merciful

beats.label: Three hundred years and nine
beats.primary: They were young men who believed in their Lord, in a place where saying so would have got them stoned. They withdrew to a cave and asked Him for one thing.

beats.label: Three hundred years and nine
beats.primary: "So We cast [a cover of sleep] over their ears within the cave for a number of years." That was the answer. Sleep.

beats.label: Three hundred years and nine
beats.primary: "And you would think them awake, while they were asleep. And We turned them to the right and to the left…" — for three hundred years, and nine.
…And ever is He, to the believers, Merciful.

beats.label: catalog id 3, verbatim in full — these are the words the youths said in the cave, Qur'ān 18:10
beats.primary: Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and guide us rightly through our affair.
beats.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا
beats.transliteration: Rabbana atina min ladunka rahmatan wa hayyi' lana min amrina rashada

beats.primary: That sentence was theirs first. They said it going in — and it was being answered the whole time they were unconscious of it, one turn at a time, for three centuries.

sources.verified: ⚠️ verified, with an excerpt boundary disclosed. Fetched: "And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and exceeded by nine." The very next ayah is 18:26 — "Say, 'Allah is most knowing of how long they remained…'" Classical readings split on whether 18:25 reports the People of the Book's figure with 18:26 as the divine qualifier. Under the majority reading the beat is fine and it is what the shipped Saheeh International text says flatly. Founder option if he prefers maximum caution: beat 5 can end at the 18:18 quotation and drop the number entirely; beat 8's "three centuries" would become "the whole time".

sources.claim: DISCLOSURE FOLDED IN AT TRANSCRIPTION — the successor of beat 5's own on-screen quotation. 18:19, the ayah immediately after 18:18, has the sleepers themselves guess wrong and be answered with the same "your Lord is most knowing how long" qualifier the deck already discloses at the farther 18:25/18:26: "And similarly, We awakened them that they might question one another. Said a speaker from among them, 'How long have you remained [here]?' They said, 'We have remained a day or part of a day.' They said, 'Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained.'" Non-blocking — no contradiction of any beat — and the founder option recorded on the 18:25 row (cut the number) resolves both instances at once.
